== Biography ==
Richard was born about 1778. He was the son of [[Glasgow-1549|John Glasgow]].  He passed away before 1859.
== Research Notes ==
=== Original Huntingdon will reviewed — 24 October 2026 ===

The original 1825 will explicitly names Richard among John’s children and gives him a $200 legacy. The existing Richard account represents the son in this same Sinking Valley family, with a compatible circa-1778 generation and later Blair County life. The original named-child clause replaces reliance on the unsourced migration narrative; that narrative’s precise Scottish birth and travel details remain unverified. The original will names wife Margaret, sons Richard, William, John, Samuel, Matthew, James and Taylor, and daughters Hannah and Jane. James and Taylor receive the 322-acre, 72-perch home tract jointly, subject to Margaret’s support and the legacies, and are appointed executors. The register records probate and the grant to both executors on 12 March 1825. The will names no mother for the children, no Hunter maiden surname, and no Scottish father for its testator. The widow Margaret is not automatically each child’s mother. The exact percentage assesses the complete father–child identification and is subjective. The original establishes the named family roles; identification of later adults, precise vital dates, maternal parentage and earlier Scottish ancestry require their own evidence. No live WikiTree save or vital-field change is made.<ref>[https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/3:1:3QS7-L99B-T8NH?cc=1999196&wc=9PM6-7MN%3A268496101%2C268530601 Huntingdon County, Pennsylvania, Wills 1822–1847, volumes 3–4, register pp. 139–140; John Glasgow of Antis Township, will 21 January 1825, proved 12 March 1825; FamilySearch, Pennsylvania Probate Records, image 103 of 607. Original full page and both page details inspected 24 October 2026.]</ref>

Earlier dated statements below retain their source context; the original-will conclusions above supersede their uninspected-source and parentage assessments.

=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

This dated review supersedes any earlier grade of this pair within the stated record scope. The existing father [[Glasgow-1549]] is assessed at 72% (probable). The published family account specifically says John and Margaret sailed in 1781 with young son Richard; the child’s circa-1778 Scottish birth and Pennsylvania life fit. The account’s source is unidentified and the cited will is uninspected.

Named child to the specific adult family role represented by the selected father; independent earlier ancestry is outside this assessment.

Next useful test: Inspect Huntingdon wills 1822–1847 vols 3–4 image 103 and continuations for named child and property links.
